4. Park Forest
The Village of Park Forest has 11,921 residents over the age of 16 who are employed. 45.4% of this number are employed in professional or managerial positions, 32% are employed at clerical or sales jobs, 14.3% are employed as craftsmen or operatives, 1.8% are farmers or laborers, and 6.5% are employed at service type jobs. 69.9% of the working population of Park Forest commute by automobile. The median family income for the Village of Park Forest is $13,951 per year. 8.8% of the families earn less than $7,000 per year, 13.2% of the families earn between $7,000 and $9,999 per year, 34.6% earn between $10,000 and $14,999 and 43.3% of the families earn $15,000 or more per year. The total assessed valuation of the land in Park Forest is $90,559,000. The aggregate tax rate per $100 valuation falls between a minimum of 7 684 and a maximum of 8.248. K. Surrounding Natural and Cultural Features
There are no known National Register of Historic Places or Landmarks involved with, nor in the area of this improvement. The State of Illinois Department of Business and Economic Development in a letter dated May 2, 1972, confirmed that "The Natural Resource Development Board has reviewed the Environmental Impact Statement" for this highway project and "has no adverse comments to make thereon." The Director of the Illinois Department of Conservation, who is the State Officer for Historic Preservation, is a member of the Natural Resource Development Board. (See Appendix "A")
The Cook County Forest Preserve District owns lands along Lincoln Highway. The proposed improvement does not require right-of-way acquisition, but will require a temporary construction easement for the purposes of removing old existing bridge wingwalls in the process of constructing a new bridge over Thorn Creek. The new bridge structure will be constructed entirely within the existing right-of-way. In order to provide the necessary hydraulic requirements on Lincoln Highway over the Thorn Creek Bridge, it is necessary to raise the profile grade on Lincoln Highway. This change in grade affects the Forest Preserve District's entrance immediately west of the Thorn Creek Bridge to the extent that it is necessary to rebuild this driveway so that a more desirable grade can be obtained. The total amount of temporary easement from the Cook County Forest Preserve is 7250 square feet or approximately 0.17 acres. (See Exhibit 8 and 9)
